metadata.summary: The event will focus on access to justice, building on the outcomes of CSW70, CEDAW General Recommendation No. 39 on the rights of Indigenous women and girls, and broader efforts to accelerate progress across the Sustainable Development Goals.
metadata.description:
The commemoration event aims to:
Celebrate the leadership and contributions of Indigenous women and girls across all regions, including as leaders, knowledge-bearers, human rights defenders, environmental defenders and agents of sustainable development.
Promote the application of CEDAW General Recommendation No. 39, building on the CSW70 Agreed Conclusions on access to justice and focusing on plural legal systems,
Promote concrete follow-up and accountability for commitments to Indigenous women and girls, including through meaningful participation, resource mobilization, sharing best practices and lessons learned, and Indigenous-led data at global, regional, national and local levels.

topics.label: Climate Justice and Territorial Rights
topics.description: Speakers connected the climate crisis with Indigenous women’s rights to land, territories, water, biodiversity, and natural resources. Indigenous women were described as frontline defenders and knowledge holders whose role in environmental stewardship and territorial protection must be respected.

topics.label: Languages, Culture, and Indigenous Knowledge
topics.description: A recurring topic was the role of Indigenous women in safeguarding languages, cultural practices, ancestral knowledge, and intergenerational memory. Speakers presented this work as central both to Indigenous identity and to broader goals such as education, biodiversity protection, and community resilience.

topics.label: Implementation of CEDAW General Recommendation 39
topics.description: CEDAW General Recommendation No. 39 was repeatedly presented as a key tool for advancing the rights of Indigenous women and girls. Speakers focused on dissemination, implementation, monitoring, and linking GR39 with broader UN commitments such as CSW70.

topics.label: Direct Funding for Indigenous Women
topics.description: Several interventions called for direct, flexible, sustained, and culturally appropriate financing for Indigenous women’s organizations and leadership. The discussion stressed that political commitments must be backed by budgets and resources, not symbolic recognition alone.

topics.label: Access to Justice and Accountability
topics.description: Many statements highlighted persistent barriers to justice for Indigenous women and girls, including weak implementation of laws and limited accountability. The discussion called for culturally and linguistically appropriate justice systems, effective remedies, and follow-up mechanisms that turn commitments into action.

topics.label: Intercultural Health and Reproductive Rights
topics.description: Health was discussed not only as access to services, but as the need for culturally appropriate and rights-based care for Indigenous women and girls. Speakers highlighted reproductive rights, informed consent, midwifery, and the harms caused by coercive or discriminatory health practices.

topics.label: Violence Against Indigenous Women and Girls
topics.description: Participants raised concerns about the multiple forms of violence faced by Indigenous women and girls, including gender-based violence, attacks on women human rights defenders, and abuses linked to discrimination and exclusion. The need for prevention, protection, justice, reparations, and survivor-centered responses was stressed.

topics.description: A major theme was the need for Indigenous women and girls to participate fully, safely, and effectively in decisions affecting their lives, communities, and territories.
